ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point $C$ is on the circle $\odot O$, point $P$ is on the extension of the diameter $AB$ of $\odot O$. Connect $AC$, $OC$, $BC$, $CP$, and it is given that $BO=BC=BP$. $CP$ is the tangent to the circle $\odot O$; If $OP=4$, find the length of $AC$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $OP=4$, and $BO=BC=BP$.\\
Therefore, $OB=OC=OA=BC=BP=2$, and $AB=4$,\\
Since $AB$ is the diameter,\\
Therefore, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
Thus, $AC=\sqrt{AB^{2}-BC^{2}}=\sqrt{4^{2}-2^{2}}=\boxed{2\sqrt{3}}$.

Connect $AC$, $OC$, $BC$, and $CP$. It is given that $BO=BC=BP$, and $CP$ is tangent to circle $\odot O$. If $OP=4$, find the length of $AC$.
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Solution: Since $OP=4$ and $BO=BC=BP$, therefore $OB=OC=OA=BC=BP=2$, and $AB=4$. Since $AB$ is the diameter, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$. Thus, $AC=\sqrt{AB^{2}-BC^{2}}=\sqrt{4^{2}-2^{2}}=\boxed{2\sqrt{3}}$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a circle with O as the center. A, O, B, P are on the same horizontal straight line, in the order A-O-B-P. A and B are the intersection points of the circle and the horizontal straight line, so AB is the diameter of the circle; P is to the right of B, and is a point on the extension line of diameter AB. C is located on the upper circumference of the circle. In the figure, AC, OC, BC, and CP are connected, where CP extends from C to P on the right, and is indicated as the tangent to the circle at point C. Reasoning: It is known that BO = BC = BP, and OP = 4. From the figure it can be seen that B is between O and P, so OP = OB + BP. Also because OB = BP, therefore 4 = OB + OB = 2OB, giving OB = BP = 2. O is the center of the circle, and A, B, C are all on the circle, so OA = OB = OC = 2, therefore diameter AB = OA + OB = 4. Because AB is the diameter of the circle and C is on the circle, according to Thales' theorem, ∠ACB = 90°. In right triangle ABC, AB is the hypotenuse, BC = 2, AB = 4, so AC = sqrt(AB^2 - BC^2) = sqrt(4^2 - 2^2) = sqrt(16 - 4) = sqrt(12) = 2√3.
